title: Conjugacy of Complements in Schur–Zassenhaus (Abelian Case)
description: Answers the parent Schur–Zassenhaus entry's first open question — the conjugacy half — in its base abelian case. Mathlib supplies only the existence half (a normal subgroup of coprime order and index has a complement); this entry proves that when the normal subgroup N is abelian, any two complements of N are conjugate, in fact by an element of N. The engine is Mathlib's QuotientDiff transfer machinery: each complement is shown to be the point-stabilizer of the corresponding transversal class, the N-action on QuotientDiff is transitive, and stabilizers of points in one orbit are conjugate. The abelian case is exactly the inductive step of the full solvable theorem.

overview.historicalContext:
The Schur–Zassenhaus theorem has two halves. The existence half (Schur 1904 for abelian kernels, Zassenhaus 1937 in general) says a normal subgroup N ⊴ G with gcd(|N|, [G:N]) = 1 has a complement. The conjugacy half says that, provided N or G/N is solvable, any two complements of N are conjugate. By the Feit–Thompson theorem one of |N|, [G:N] is odd hence (Feit–Thompson) the corresponding factor is solvable, so the conjugacy half in fact holds unconditionally — but its proof reduces, by induction along a chief series, to the abelian case proved here.

The abelian case is the cohomological heart of the theorem. Complements of an abelian normal N correspond to 1-cocycles of G/N with values in N modulo coboundaries, i.e. to the cohomology group H¹(G/N, N); coprimality of |N| and [G:N] forces this group to vanish, which says precisely that all complements lie in a single conjugacy class. Mathlib encodes this vanishing in its 'diff' transfer machinery: the quotient set N.QuotientDiff of left transversals modulo the diff relation carries a transitive N-action exactly when |N| is coprime to its index (Subgroup.exists_smul_eq).

Mathlib formalizes only the existence half (Subgroup.exists_right_complement'_of_coprime). This entry adds the conjugacy half for abelian N, which is the inductive engine of the general solvable result.
overview.problemStatement: Let N be a finite abelian normal subgroup of a finite group G with gcd(|N|, [G:N]) = 1. Prove that any two complements of N are conjugate — and conjugate by an element of N — so that, together with the existence half, the complements of N form a single N-conjugacy class.
overview.proofStrategy: Mathlib already proves the cohomological core: the N-action on the set N.QuotientDiff of left transversals (mod the diff relation) is transitive when the orders are coprime (exists_smul_eq), and each point-stabilizer is a complement of N (isComplement'_stabilizer_of_coprime). The missing direction is that EVERY complement arises as a point-stabilizer. We supply it as follows. A complement K, viewed as a subset of G, is a left transversal of N, giving a point complementPoint K ∈ N.QuotientDiff. Since K is a subgroup, right-translating the set K by any k ∈ K leaves it unchanged, so K ⊆ stabilizer G (complementPoint K). But that stabilizer is itself a complement, hence has order [G:N] = |K|; equal finite cardinalities with an inclusion force stabilizer G (complementPoint K) = K. Now for two complements K₁, K₂, transitivity gives h ∈ N with h • complementPoint K₁ = complementPoint K₂, and stabilizer_smul_eq_stabilizer_map_conj converts this orbit relation into K₂ = K₁ conjugated by h ∈ N.
keyInsights: Conjugacy of complements for abelian N is the statement H¹(G/N, N) = 0, and coprimality of |N| with [G:N] is exactly what makes this cohomology vanish.
Mathlib's QuotientDiff machinery already packages the vanishing as transitivity of the N-action (exists_smul_eq); the only missing piece is the bijection complements ↔ point-stabilizers.

That bijection is obtained cheaply by a cardinality argument: one easy inclusion K ⊆ stabilizer (right-translation invariance of a subgroup) plus the fact that both sides are complements of equal order [G:N].
Conjugacy then drops out of a general group-action lemma: stabilizers of two points in the same orbit are conjugate by any group element carrying one to the other — here an element of N.
The abelian case is not a special curiosity: it is precisely the inductive step that proves the full solvable (hence, via Feit–Thompson, unconditional) conjugacy half.

sections.title: Section I: Complements as Points of QuotientDiff
sections.summary: complementTransversal and complementPoint exhibit a complement K as a left transversal of N and hence a point of N.QuotientDiff. le_stabilizer_complementPoint proves K ≤ stabilizer G (complementPoint K) — the only place subgroup-hood of K is used — by showing each k ∈ K right-fixes the set K, so it fixes the transversal class.
sections.mathContext: Each complement determines a canonical point of the transfer space N.QuotientDiff and is contained in that point's stabilizer.

sections.title: Section II: Stabilizer = Complement, and Conjugacy
sections.summary: stabilizer_complementPoint_eq upgrades the inclusion to equality by a cardinality argument (the stabilizer is also a complement, so both have order [G:N]). isComplement'_conj_of_isMulCommutative combines transitivity of the N-action (exists_smul_eq) with stabilizer_smul_eq_stabilizer_map_conj to conjugate any two complements by an element of N. exists_and_conj packages this with Mathlib's existence half.
sections.mathContext: Every complement is a point-stabilizer; transitivity of the orbit makes all complements N-conjugate, so they form a single conjugacy class.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) formalization, in 141 lines with 4 theorems and 2 definitions, of the conjugacy half of Schur–Zassenhaus in the abelian case: for an abelian normal subgroup N of coprime order and index, any two complements are conjugate by an element of N, and the complements form a single N-conjugacy class. The cohomological core (transitivity of the QuotientDiff action) is invoked from Mathlib; the complement↔stabilizer correspondence and the conjugacy conclusion are proved here.
conclusion.implications: This answers the abelian base case of the parent entry's first open question — the harder, conjugacy direction of Schur–Zassenhaus, which Mathlib does not provide. Conjugacy is what gives uniqueness of the semidirect-product splitting up to inner automorphism, the missing ingredient for using Schur–Zassenhaus in small-order group classification. The abelian case proved here is exactly the inductive step from which the full solvable (hence, by Feit–Thompson, unconditional) conjugacy half follows.
openQuestions: Promote the abelian case to the general solvable case by induction along a chief series of N (or of G/N), each step invoking the abelian conjugacy proved here.
Derive uniqueness-up-to-isomorphism of the semidirect product G = N ⋊ K from conjugacy of complements, and connect it to the classification of groups of small order.

mainTheorems.name: stabilizer_complementPoint_eq
mainTheorems.description: Converse of the Schur–Zassenhaus construction: every complement K of an abelian normal N of coprime order/index is the stabilizer of its corresponding point of N.QuotientDiff — identifying complements with fixed points of the N-action.
mainTheorems.leanType: (hN : Nat.Coprime (Nat.card N) N.index) → (h : IsComplement' N K) → stabilizer G (complementPoint h) = K

mainTheorems.name: le_stabilizer_complementPoint
mainTheorems.description: Each k ∈ K fixes the transversal point complementPoint h: right-translating the subset K by one of its own elements leaves it invariant. The single step that uses that K is a subgroup, giving K ≤ stabilizer G (complementPoint h).
